messages:
alice_ops: Seeing a spike in egress QPS to the CDN from eu2 and the cloud peering is hitting soft-throttles. GPU attach times ballooning, some provisioning requests are failing with 504s. Anyone else?
ben_infra: Confirmed — logs show sustained BGP path flaps and provider is rate-limiting peering. A subset of interconnects to our eu2 POP are showing 30-40% packet loss for short bursts. GPU pools in eu2 are reporting attach latency >120s.
carmen_oncall: Impact: hosted inference requests in eu2 showing elevated queuing and a handful of canaries timed out. No customer-facing outage yet but error budget for several teams will burn if this persists.
sasha_eng: Workaround idea: shift traffic for sensitive low-latency routes to eu-central (eu1), and divert bulk async/batch workloads to us-west to reduce cross-region egress. Can we do a targeted routing policy change?
b en_infra: I'll open the routing shim: we can create a temporary policy that routes by route tag `latency-sensitive` -> eu1, `bulk` -> us-west. Will take ~8-12m to propagate. Command I'm running:```bash
# apply temporary route policy
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/route-policies" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"name":"peering-eu2-evac","rules":[{"match":"route.tags contains \"latency-sensitive\"","target":"eu1"},{"match":"route.tags contains \"bulk\"","target":"us-west"}]}'
```
deploy-bot: Routing policy `peering-eu2-evac` created and queued for rollout. Canary to 5% started. :rocket:
tom_prod_sre: Start the canary but hold full shift until we confirm attach latency drops and no cross-region egress billing surprises. Monitor GPU attach histogram and egress meter. Also notify billing.
alice_ops: Good call. I'm enabling prefix KV cache for chat sessions in eu2 so the ones that remain there have lower attach frequency: `runtime.cache.prefix_enable=true` for the chat route. That reduces attach spikes by ~60%.
sasha_eng: For provisioning failures: add a backoff to the GPU provisioner so it retries with jitter and does not flood the provider control plane. Patch ready:```go
// exponential backoff with jitter
func provisionWithBackoff(req Request) error {
  return backoff.Retry(func() error { return provision(req) }, backoff.WithJitter(backoff.NewExponentialBackOff(), 0.2))
}
```
ben_infra: Also flagged KMS latencies — the provider's KMS fronting that we use for ephemeral DEK wrapping is showing increased RPC p95. For short-term, we can serve cached wrapped keys for existing sessions (we already do for 1h) and extend to 2h for affected clusters. Doing key cache extension for eu2 nodes now.
carmen_oncall: Extending cache TTL to 2h applied to eu2 private nodes. Will add audit entry and manual rotation note. Security OK with approval from sec.
tom_prod_sre: Billing note: cross-region egress cost estimate for full shift ~ +12% for next 24h. If we keep mixed routing (sensitive -> eu1, bulk -> us-west) expected delta ~ +3-4%. Call with finance if we go full-shift.
alice_ops: Canary metrics: after 7m, canary error rate in eu2 reduced from 0.9% to 0.15%. GPU attach p50 down from 90s -> 18s for canary traffic.
sasha_eng: Great. I'll merge the provisioner backoff change to canary branch and roll to eu2 provisioner pool.
deploy-bot: Provisioner service rollout started (canary). Image: registry.redwood/infra/provisioner:v2.3.1-canary
ben_infra: Provider issued mitigation: they're rehoming some peering sessions and we see fewer flaps. But p95 still elevated. Keep routing policy for now.
carmen_oncall: ETA from provider: 2 hours to finish reroute. Agree to keep partial shift and monitor.
tom_prod_sre: Postmortem owners: @ben_infra, @alice_ops, @sasha_eng. Please capture RCA, timeline, cost impact, and any automation to detect and auto-shift on similar peering throttles.
alice_ops: Will add automation ticket to runbook: auto-detect peering QPS surge -> create `peering-evac` route and start canary.
sasha_eng: Also add abort criteria: if cross-region egress > X% or error rate increases in target region, rollback.
ben_infra: For completeness: rolling a small VM-level tweak to reduce connection churn (tcp_retries2 and keepalive) on eu2 provision nodes; should reduce reconnections to provider. Applying now.
carmen_oncall: Monitoring: added dashboard at https://mon.redwood/internal/d/peering-eu2 showing attach latency, egress bytes, provider announced routes. Watch that for next 3 hours.
alice_ops: Update: provider reports final peering convergence completed. We're seeing attach times stable and can scale back routing policy in 30m if metrics hold.
tom_prod_sre: OK to start gradual rollback of `peering-eu2-evac` after 30m stable window. Keep KV cache extension until tomorrow morning.
carmen_oncall: Incident status -> mitigated. Will start full write-up and timeline. Closing thread when postmortem link posted. :white_check_mark:
